title: {{term:counting}} and comparing to 10
summary: Match apples one to one, count them and compare. Then meet the signs <, > and =.
guide: This studio is for Year 1. Your child works with apples and counters and answers by tapping a number or a sign. If they can't read yet, read the sentences to them.
It starts with matching: one apple for each place. Even without counting, a child can see which group has more. Then they count into a ten-frame; a row holds 5, so 7 is "5 and 2 more".
Finally two rows are compared with <, > or =. The open mouth of the sign always faces the bigger number.

engine.instruction-ring: Circle the apples with no partner.

match.title: One apple on each plate
match.prompt: Put just one apple on each plate. How many apples are left over?
match.hint: Tap an apple to put it on a plate. When every plate has one, count the apples that are left.
match.success: Well done! 2 apples are left over. There were more apples than plates.
match.why: Without counting, how did you know there were more apples?
match.model: Every plate got one apple and there were still apples left. So there are more apples. You don't need to count to compare: matching is enough.

feedback.too-few: There is still an empty plate. Put one apple on it.
feedback.too-many: There is still an empty plate. Put one apple on it.
feedback.counted-all: 8 is all the apples. Count only the apples that are not on a plate.
feedback.counted-placed: 6 are on the plates. Count the apples that didn't fit.
feedback.too-big: Count the apples that are not on a plate again.
feedback.too-small: Count the apples that are not on a plate again.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

count-frame.title: Count and build
count-frame.prompt: Count the apples. Put the same number in the ten-frame. Then tap the number.
count-frame.hint: One row of the frame has 5 spaces. Fill one row. How many more do you need?
count-frame.success: Well done! 7 apples: one row of 5 and 2 more.
count-frame.why: In the ten-frame, how can you tell it's 7 without counting one by one?
count-frame.model: The top row is full, so that's 5. There are 2 in the bottom row. 5 and 2 make 7.

feedback.too-many: Too many in the frame. Tap an apple to take it away.
feedback.too-few: Too few in the frame. Count the apples on the plate again.
feedback.too-big: That number is too big. Count the apples in the frame.
feedback.too-small: That number is too small. Count the apples in the frame.
feedback.empty: Now tap the number for your answer.

who-has-more.title: Who has more?
who-has-more.prompt: Ali has 5 apples. Maryam has 8 apples. Circle Maryam's apples with no partner. Tap the bigger number.
who-has-more.hint: Each of Ali's apples pairs with the apple under it. Which of Maryam's apples have no partner?
who-has-more.success: Well done! 8 is more than 5. Maryam has 3 more apples.
who-has-more.why: If Maryam's apples were big and Ali's were tiny, would Maryam still have more? Why?
who-has-more.model: Yes. We compare how many, not how big. Maryam has 3 apples with no partner, so she has more apples.

feedback.marked-too-few: There's still an apple with no partner. Which of Maryam's apples has no apple of Ali's above it?
feedback.marked-too-many: You circled an apple that has a partner. Tap it again.
feedback.picked-smaller: 5 is Ali's number. Ali has fewer. Tap the bigger number.
feedback.picked-extra: 3 is how many have no partner. We want the bigger number: how many apples does Maryam have?

signs.title: <, > or =
signs.prompt: Sara has 6 apples. Reza has 9 apples. Which one is right?
signs.hint: The open mouth of the sign faces the bigger number. The point faces the smaller one.
signs.why: If we swap 6 and 9, which sign do you use? Why?
signs.model: 9 > 6. The mouth still opens towards 9, because 9 is bigger.

feedback.wrong: Match the apples. Who has more? The open mouth of the sign must face their number.
